classification.difficultyReason: Select decreasing distance from home and combine the supplied initial distance/speed into a familiar linear model; draw the finite domain and interpret its two parameters.

content.prompt: A man is walking home at $6$ km/h. He starts at a point $18$ km from his home. Draw a graph representing his trip home. State the gradient and vertical axis intercept, and give a formula that describes the trip.

answer.short: Gradient $-6$ km/h; vertical intercept $18$ km; $d=18-6t$, $0\le t\le3$, with t in hours and d in kilometres.
answer.worked: Let t be the time in hours after he starts and d his distance in kilometres from home. Initially $d=18$. Each hour the distance decreases by 6 km, so $d=18-6t$. The gradient is $-6$ km/h and the vertical intercept is 18 km. He reaches home when $0=18-6t$, giving $t=3$. Draw the line segment from $(0,18)$ to $(3,0)$, valid for $0\le t\le3$.

spec.description: Distance from HOME decreases linearly from18km to0 over3hours. Axis units explicit and finite physical trip domain preserved.
